lessons.c:
Your final project is an automated conveyor sorting system. Inputs: start, stop, entry sensor, size sensor. Outputs: conveyor motor, diverter, alarm lamp.

Start by writing the requirements and an I/O list, then plan the states: idle, running and fault.
lessons.x: Large boxes go to the left lane, small boxes continue straight on.
lessons.ex: Write the I/O list and the requirements for your sorter.
q: It sends a signal into the PLC.
It is driven by the PLC.
These cover normal and abnormal operation.

lessons.c: Detect each product with a rising edge at the entry sensor, classify it using the size sensor, and count each category with a counter. Debounce noisy signals first.
lessons.x: Each large box adds to nLarge and each small box to nSmall.
lessons.ex: Add a reset button that clears both counts.

lessons.c: Use a state machine with Idle, Running and Fault. The diverter must move after the box travels from the sensor to the diverter, so use a TON for that travel time.
lessons.x: A large box is seen, a 2-second timer runs, then the diverter pushes it off.
lessons.ex: Estimate the travel time from belt speed and distance.

lessons.c:
Detect faults such as a jam (a sensor stuck on too long), a motor overload and an emergency stop. Latch alarms, stop the conveyor, and light the alarm lamp.

Provide a reset button that only works once the cause has cleared.
lessons.x: A sensor stays on for 10 seconds, a timeout trips, the belt stops and the lamp lights.
lessons.ex: List three possible faults and how each is detected.
